title: Introduce time-windowed anchored sample prioritizer and gradual-rolloff CI hook
author: Aditi Rao
description: Summary: Add a time-windowed anchored sample prioritizer and a gradual-rolloff CI hook to reduce noisy regressions driven by temporal shifts in prompt traffic. Motivation: Prompt sets in production show time-dependent distribution shifts; CI gates that treat recent and old examples equally either overreact to transient blips or mask slow degradations. This change introduces a prioritizer that weights samples by recency and by an 'anchor' stability score, plus a CI hook that applies a configurable gradual-rolloff policy when a regression signal is detected. Implementation: - New prioritizer: hooks/time_windowed_prioritizer.py implements a sliding-window prioritization algorithm with parameters window_days, recency_decay_rate, and anchor_weight. Anchors are maintained per-cohort using a lightweight rolling-stats store and are used to stabilize sample selection. - CI hook: hooks/gradual_rolloff_hook.py integrates with the existing eval-runner to convert a binary fail into a staged rollout: stage 1 (soft warning), stage 2 (partial gate: block only high-risk release channels), stage 3 (block full merge) with automatic backoff and a manual override. - Telemetry: metrics/telemetry_mappings.yaml and runtime instrumentation emit new signals: prioritizer.sample_weights, anchor.stability_score, ci.rolloff_stage, and ci.rolloff_trigger_reason. - CLI/Config: eval_harness.cli accepts --prioritizer-window and --rolloff-policy flags; default behavior preserves existing deterministic sampling unless explicitly enabled. - Tests and docs: tests/test_time_prioritizer.py covers algorithmic invariants; integration/eval_smoke uses a synthetic time-series corpus to validate staged rolloff behavior; docs/guides/temporal-prioritizer.md documents rationale and tuning knobs. Backwards compatibility: defaults keep prior behavior. Rollout plan: feature flag gated; start with internal canary on nightly runs, then opt-in on release branches. Checklist: - [x] unit tests - [x] integration smoke - [x] telemetry mapping - [x] docs - [x] feature flag gating - [x] Linear tickets updated.
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial prioritizer prototype; integrate with eval runner and CI hook; add tests, telemetry, and docs.
review_conversation: Liam O'Connor: Nice concise algorithm. Curious about worst-case cost when window_days is large; can we add an evict strategy?
Aditi Rao: Added an eviction policy with max_window_items and lazy compaction; updated tests to assert memory bounds.
Priya Kapoor: CI rollout stages look sensible. Suggest recording the list of blocked commits for auditability.
Aditi Rao: Added ci.rolloff_blocked_commits telemetry and a small audit log file for private deployments.
Omar Haddad: Integration test flaky on first run due to clock skew in the CI runner; recommended using a fixed-seed time provider.
Aditi Rao: Switched tests to a deterministic fake clock; re-ran integration and tests are stable.
Priya Kapoor: Approving after minor nits (doc phrasing).
merge_outcome: Merged to main after approvals and CI green. Feature gated behind 'temporal_prioritizer' flag for staged rollout.
release_notes: Adds a time-windowed sample prioritizer for evals and a gradual-rolloff CI hook to reduce noise from temporal prompt shifts. Telemetry keys: prioritizer.sample_weights, anchor.stability_score, ci.rolloff_stage. Backwards compatible by default.
notes: This PR targets reducing false positives in prompt regression gates by biasing evaluation samples toward recent, yet stable, examples. Ops: recommend enabling telemetry in canary runs and monitoring ci.rolloff_stage over two weeks before broader rollouts.
